status_reason: A dairy-precedented NIR concept can be shortlisted, but the turbidity behaviour and protein range are not yet characterised, so the technique split remains conditional.

premise_checks.premise: A single probe geometry can handle both the clear and the turbid states of the whey stream.
premise_checks.explanation: In the dairy example a transflection probe is reported to work for both low-fat and high-fat products in some cases; this is a precedent to test, not proof for this stream.

premise_checks.premise: NIR spectroscopy can track protein in dairy streams in-line.
premise_checks.explanation: Published dairy examples quantify fat and protein with NIR reflection and transmission plus PLS; this motivates a test on the customer's whey, it does not prove performance there.

recommendations.rationale: NIR is the standard fiber-optic online method for dairy liquids, and transflection is reported in the dairy example to serve both low-fat and high-fat products in some cases. Pathlength must be controlled because too wide a gap loses signal to water absorption.
recommendations.conditions: Tested across the full clear-to-turbid range seen in operation; if the turbid state saturates the signal, add the reflection route (M2).

citations.quote: In some cases, a Transflection probe can already be a combined solution working well for low-fat and high-fat containing milk products.
the precise control of the optical pathlength (usually 1 - 10 mm); if the pathlength is too wide, the signal is lost to absorption; if too narrow, the sample represents a negligible volume.
Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.

recommendations.rationale: NIR reflection is the dairy-precedented geometry for opaque or highly concentrated products, so it is the natural fallback for the turbid state. Its signals are sensitive to surface and particle characteristics, so scatter correction and a matrix-specific calibration are needed.
recommendations.conditions: Tested on turbid samples from the same process states used for M1, using the same NIR spectrometer and light source.

citations.quote: NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.
the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.
NIR Spectrometer and NIR light source remain the same for both reflection and transmission techniques.

recommendations.rationale: Raman tolerates water far better than infrared absorption and gives molecular specificity, so it is a candidate if NIR cannot separate protein from the changing background. Its weak signals and possible fluorescence background must be checked on real whey.
recommendations.conditions: Only if the NIR trials (M1, M2) fail to track protein across the turbidity change.

citations.quote: Raman is particularly well-suited for aqueous environments, as it exhibits low absorbance for water molecules compared to infrared methods.
superposition of luminescence (fluorescence), which has a significantly higher intensity.

recommendations.rationale: A transmission signal saturates once the liquid becomes turbid or optically dense, which is exactly the condition the concept must handle. UV-Vis mixture signals also overlap strongly, giving low selectivity for protein in a real whey matrix.

citations.quote: transmission setup becomes saturated because the light cannot penetrate the bulk of the sample.
the strong overlap of spectral signals in UV spectra complicates the analysis of real samples

steps.step: Collect representative whey samples spanning the full clear-to-turbid range and the expected protein variation, including samples from the operating conditions that cause turbidity.
steps.purpose: Cover the chemical and physical variation the in-line model must handle.

steps.step: Measure each sample with the laboratory reference protein method under a defined protocol.
steps.purpose: Provide independent reference values for calibration and validation.

steps.step: Record NIR transflection spectra (M1) on all samples first, then NIR reflection spectra (M2) on the same samples with the same spectrometer and light source.
steps.purpose: Compare the single-method candidates on identical samples before any combined use.

steps.step: Build PLS calibration models per technique with scatter-appropriate preprocessing, and validate on held-out samples or a separate production run not used in calibration.
steps.purpose: Estimate real prediction error rather than calibration fit.

feasibility_plan.reference_measurements: Laboratory protein results on every calibration and validation sample, as the customer stated.
feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Customer-defined accuracy across both the clear and turbid states; not met by either technique alone means re-testing with the other technique or reconsidering M3.

Laboratory protein analysis is available for all calibration samples.

chemometrics_note: A PLS regression per technique is the starting point; scatter-sensitive preprocessing (e.g. MSC or SNV) should be tested against the turbidity variation, and the model must be validated on held-out runs spanning both optical states.
realtime_tracking_note: The goal is continuous in-line tracking of protein as the stream changes; acquisition conditions should allow spectra fast enough to follow the concentration dynamics before the concentration stage.
future_direction: If NIR alone cannot separate protein from the turbidity-driven background, a Raman channel (M3) on the same sampling point is the next extension to test.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the turbidity episodes are rare or mild, O1 alone may suffice; if transflection fails across the turbid state or protein selectivity is poor, the Raman conditional (M3) enters the comparison.
proposal.next_step: Run the feasibility trial on representative clear and turbid whey samples with laboratory protein references, testing transflection and reflection with the same NIR spectrometer.

brief_answer: Test NIR first: a transflection probe on the clear whey, with an NIR reflection channel evaluated in parallel for the turbid state, since both dairy-precedented techniques can share one NIR spectrometer. UV-Vis transmission is not recommended because it saturates when the stream turns turbid. Open points: the protein range and accuracy needed, what causes the turbidity, and the installation conditions decide the final configuration.
